newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P lowers Burns Philp to BBB/A3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P lowers Burns Philp to BBB/A3.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Friday that it lowered the ratings on food ingredients group Burns Philp and Co Ltd to BBB/A3 from BBB-plus/A2.
The ratings agency also said the company's ratings had been placed on creditwatch negative.

S&P said the Sydney-based company's current and future operating performance was not consistent with the higher long term rating, even after the planned sale of the herbs and spice businesses in North America and Europe.

"Meanwhile, the company's weak financial profile has been exacerbated by the recent announcement of the settlement of the Estate Mortgage claims, which includes A$90 million cash payment by BPC," it said.

"The settlement has eliminated the uncertainty of the litigation faced by BPC, but has crystallised the magnitude of cash outflow at a time when BPC's operating performance and financial parameters are vulnerable for the ratings."
S&P said the ratings would remain on creditwatch until the asset sales had been concluded, reflecting uncertainties aboutits capacity to meet debt service obligations from the reduced asset base.
"In the short term, before successful completion of the planned asset sale, write-downs in asset value may cause BPC to seek covenant renegotiation," it said.
Over the medium term, however, the company should have its financial position restored and be able to achieve its restructuring.

The S&P statement coincided with the company's announcement that it had appointed Tom Degnan to replace Ian Clack as managing director from September 1 this year. Degnan was an executive with U.S.-based Universal Foods Corp.
